cyclingpower

Compare the readings of two or three power meters that recorded the same riding. Reads FIT, GPX and CSV files, puts them on a common clock, and reports how far apart the meters are overall and across the power range. A third meter can be linked in through a bridge meter common to both sessions.

Installation 

remotes::install_github("jzuccollo/cyclingpower")

FIT files need FITfileR, which is not on CRAN. It is declared in Remotes: so the command above fetches it. GPX and CSV need nothing extra. Install dependencies with:

install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "DT", "shinyFiles"))

Usage

Name your files <run>_<source>, so run1_kickr.fit is the Kickr’s recording of run one, and pass read_rides() the directory.

library(cyclingpower)

aligned <- read_rides("rides") |> align_rides()

power_agreement(aligned)      # overall difference, in watts and per cent
# run1: assioma reads 2.6% higher than kickr (95% CI 2.4 to 2.7, from 1,800 seconds)

agreement_by_level(aligned)   # the same, across the power range
chain_sources(aligned)        # meters linked through a common bridge meter

Where the filenames do not carry the labels, build the table yourself with ride_spec_from_names() or by hand and pass that instead. compare_report() runs the whole pipeline and writes an HTML report:

compare_report("rides", "power-comparison.html")

To see an example, run demo_rides() and follow vignette("cyclingpower").

The app

launch_app() opens a local web interface with the same pipeline: pick a directory, fix the run and source labels if the filenames don’t carry them, and adjust settings. Load demo rides builds a worked example with known errors planted, also available outside the app from demo_rides().

The app can also record the meters itself over Web Bluetooth (Chrome or Edge, Record tab). The radio has no automated tests, so check the first session against a head unit you trust.

Recording

If each meter records to its own head unit, then on every unit: record every second (not “smart” recording), turn auto-pause off, let the clock set from GPS, and zero the meter after a warm-up. Ride four to six short surges from coasting so align_rides() has features to cross-correlate, then five or six steady steps across the power range so agreement_by_level() has time in each bin.

Recording in the app fixes the alignment problem, so you only need an erg ladder up and back down, with enough time at each level. However, it’s worth keeping a short block of surges anyway, just in case.

vignette("recording_rides") has a ride protocol and can export a .zwo for you to ride in erg.

Why alignment matters

Independent head units can differ by several seconds. Differencing on nominal timestamps then compares one moment’s power against another’s, which inflates the spread and shifts the mean difference.

align_rides() recovers the offset by cross-correlating the power traces. The main challenge is where a turbo ride is too steady to lock onto it. Then it will say so and fall back to the recorded timestamps.

Chaining a third meter (bridging)

Run one carries meters A and B, run two carries B and C, and you want A against C. B is the bridge and each run gives a gain relative to it, so the difference between those gains is A against C. chain_sources() marks these as chained rather than direct, because they assume B read the same on both days. chain_report() calculates and reports whether the two runs covered comparable power.
